newsitem.title: USA: Motorola wins $58 mln China cellular deal.
newsitem.headline: Motorola wins $58 mln China cellular deal.

text.p: Motorola Inc's Cellular Infrastructure Group said Monday it won a $58 million contract to expand the digital Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM) cellular telephone network in China's Hunan Province.

Under the terms of the agreement with Hunan Posts and Telecommunications Administration (Hunan PTA), the current GSM network will increase to 430,000 from 75,000 subscribers, making it Motorola's largest GSM network in China. The project is expected to be completed by the end of 1997. Motorola CIG installed Hunan PTA's original GSM network in June, 1996.

Hunan PTA will use Motorola's latest GSM microcellular base station, the M-Cell city. Other base stations will be installed, and a large number of those currently in use will be upgraded, the company said.
GSM is a digital cellular standard based.
Motorola provides wireless communications, semiconductors and advanced electronic systems, components and services.
